prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology and active forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: GLP-1 is the one candidate that combines a conceptually clean physiological discovery (the incretin effect, the identity of the active truncated peptide, proglucagon-derived peptide biology) with a therapeutic consequence of very large scale: type 2 diabetes, obesity, and now cardiovascular and renal benefit shown in large independent randomized trials. All six of us ranked it in our top two, and the physiology-centred trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the configuration every member independently proposed. The science is mature and replicated, and recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the genuine weakness. Knudsen's medicinal chemistry made liraglutide and semaglutide possible, and omitting her to stay within three names will be read as favouring academic discovery over development. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide against Habener-group work, who is not in the credited names, is not settled by the material we have. A prize that is clinically the most obvious may also be the one most open to a credit dispute.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked the unfolded protein response first for its conceptual originality and clean two-person credit (Walter and Mori), and placed GLP-1 second mainly because of the contested allocation.
responses.response: I agree that B002 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and I ranked it too low in my opening (eighth); the evidence of five top-three placements makes me move it up to my first alternative. I still would not put it ahead of GLP-1. Its medical consequence is so far mostly conceptual, and an attribution problem that can be handled by choosing the discovery-side trio is a smaller defect than a weaker link to human disease. If the committee finds the Drucker-Holst-Mojsov split indefensible, B002 is where I would go.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, proposed a trio for optogenetics of Deisseroth, Hegemann and Miesenboeck, accepting that Nagel, Bamberg and Boyden would be left out, and warned that the contested credit might delay a prize.
responses.response: I share the worry that six claimants cannot be reduced to three without a visible omission, and I think that argues for waiting rather than for the Miesenboeck variant. Replacing Nagel with Miesenboeck separates the channelrhodopsin discovery from the people who first showed it as a channel, which is the core molecular finding. If B004 is chosen I would keep Hegemann and Nagel with Deisseroth. Even so, its fit to a medicine prize is weaker than that of GLP-1, because its payoff is mainly as a research tool.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked GLP-1 first and treated Knudsen as an industrial drug-development contributor whose credit is better recognised through a therapeutic route, and also ranked anti-TNF (B006) fifth.
responses.response: I agree that the three-person basic-science trio is the right reading of the discovery, and that is also my configuration. I disagree somewhat with the suggestion that Knudsen's work could simply be recognised later through another route; no other shortlisted item covers it, and I do not want us to treat the omission as costless. On B006, which we both ranked, I think its maturity is complete but the anti-TNF principle has been recognised through antibody and cytokine work already, so I do not put it in the top configuration.

responses.point: Linnarsson named the exclusion of Knudsen, and of Habener who is outside the credited names, as a real fairness problem, and suggested that basic discovery and drug development might be better treated as separate recognitions.
responses.response: I take this seriously. A two-part configuration would let Knudsen be credited, but under the three-person cap it would force out two of the three physiology laureates, which seems a worse distortion of the discovery history. I would therefore keep a single physiology part and state the omission openly in the committee's reasoning, rather than split the achievement.

responses.point: Sandberg stressed that credit is the hard part for GLP-1, that Mojsov's identification of the active form is decisive but contested, and chose the physiology-centred trio.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and with calling Mojsov's role contested. Our shared uncertainty is that none of us can verify the priority question from the supplied material, so I would want the credit paragraph for Mojsov checked against primary publications before the final vote, and I would not make the prize depend on her inclusion if the evidence turned out weaker than we recall.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 form has priority over the Habener-group work, and whether Habener should be considered even though not among the credited names.
Whether the committee will accept omitting Knudsen's drug-development role, or prefer a configuration that includes it.
Whether the strong broad support for the unfolded protein response should displace GLP-1 if attribution to Mojsov proves unsafe.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy are still being characterized.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the shortlisted credited names appears among my recorded co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson) or affiliations. My autoimmunity and Ro52/TRIM21 field is not the topic of any preferred or alternative item.
